items.title: 'Nobody wants it': Lettuce prices see record-setting plunge as cyclospora spooks consumers
items.body: Lettuce prices posted their sharpest month-over-month decline on record as diners reconsider the vegetable amid the cyclospora outbreak.

items.title: U.S. budget deficit surged in July to highest level since March 2021
items.body: Beyond the big single-month jump, the collective red ink over the 10 months of the fiscal year rose to nearly $1.8 trillion, surpassing the same period in 2025.

items.title: Here are five key takeaways from the July CPI inflation report
items.body: Readings for July on the prices consumers pay for goods and services came in pretty much on target.

items.title: AI’s costly build-out complicates the Fed’s inflation fight
items.body: Tech leaders say AI will drive down costs. But slow corporate adoption and the data center build-out create inflation pressures that complicate the Fed’s job.

items.title: Consumer prices rose 0.1% in July, as expected, putting the annual rate at 3.4%
items.body: The consumer price index was expected to increase 0.1% in July, with an annual rate of 3.4%.

items.title: An inflation report Wednesday should be a big deal for the Fed. Here's what to expect
items.body: The consumer price index is expected to show only a modest increase for July.

items.title: U.S. economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls were projected to increase by 83,000 in July while the unemployment rate would hold steady at 4.2%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

items.title: Here are three key takeaways from the disappointing July jobs report
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls in the U.S. unexpectedly declined in July, but so did the unemployment rate, leaving investors with mixed signals.
